collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks an adult)

collection.description: A villager forgets a carefully practiced goodbye speech as a beloved guest leaves: say it anyway, or just hug.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: A traveler from another village has been staying in (name1)'s hut for a whole moon, and they leave at dawn. (name1) has prepared a short speech. It mentions the evenings by the fire, the terrible joke about the eel, and how the hut is going to feel too big. (He/she) has practiced it four times. Now the traveler is standing at the door with a bundle, and every word of it has gone.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (name1) gives up on words and hugs the traveler instead. That works too. The traveler walks off into the grey morning, turning round twice to wave. Later, sitting in the too-big hut, (name1) remembers the whole speech perfectly. (He/she) says it out loud to the empty room, just so it has been said.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "I had a speech," (name1) says. "It was very good. There was a part about the eel." The traveler starts laughing, and then (name1) does too, and the speech comes back in pieces, out of order, with the eel in the middle. It is much better that way. The traveler hugs (him/her) for a long time before leaving.
